{{nihongo|'''Ono Shrine'''|小野神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Sagami Province]].

{{commons category|Category:Ono-jinja (Atsugi)}}
[[ja:小野神社 (厚木市)]]

{{wikidata link|Q17225921|commons|Category:Ono-jinja (Atsugi)|ja|小野神社 (厚木市)|check_date=2026-05-18}}

== Overview ==
[[File:Ono-jin (Atsugi) 1.jpg|thumb|270px|Torii and haiden]]
'''Ono Shrine''' (小野神社, おのじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|lt=Shinto shrine|lt_ja=神社}} at Ono, {{ill|Atsugi, Kanagawa|ja|厚木市|lt=Atsugi|lt_ja=厚木市}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県|lt=Kanagawa Prefecture|lt_ja=神奈川県}}. It is held to be one of the {{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Sagami Province|ja|相模国の式内社一覧|lt=Shikinaisha of Sagami Province|lt_ja=相模国の式内社}} (small shrines) recorded in the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|lt=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|lt_ja=延喜式神名帳}}'' of {{ill|Enchō|ja|延長 (日本)|lt=Enchō|lt_ja=延長}} 5 (927). Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|lt=modern shrine ranking system|lt_ja=近代社格制度}} it was a {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|lt=district shrine|lt_ja=郷社}}. Its founding date is unknown; the main sanctuary is in {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|lt=shinmei-zukuri|lt_ja=神明造}}, and the annual festival is on 21 April. It was also called Shizuka Myōjin-sha, and in the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|lt=Edo period|lt_ja=江戸時代}} Shizuka Daimyōjin.

== Deities ==
* {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|lt=Yamato Takeru no Mikoto|lt_ja=日本武命}}
* ({{ill|Ame-no-Shitaharu|ja|天下春命|lt=Ame-no-Shitaharu no Mikoto|lt_ja=天下春命}})

== History ==
The shrine's founding date is unknown, but it is an old shrine of Ono: the ''Engishiki Jinmyōchō'' records it as "Ono Shrine, the one seat of Aikō District, among the thirteen seats (Shikinaisha) of Sagami Province".<ref name="chigasaki13-onojin">[http://chigasaki-family.sakura.ne.jp/photo/sagami-13sya/ono-jinjya/ono-jinjya.html Ono Shrine] (Chigasaki Kazoku: Sagami thirteen shrines) {{Broken link|date=2021-10}}</ref> The area has long been called "Ono no Sato" and was the centre of Tamagawa township in Aikō District, which appears in the ''{{ill|Wamyō Ruijushō|ja|和名類聚抄|lt=Wamyō Ruijushō|lt_ja=和名類聚抄}}''. The shrine's tradition says that in {{ill|Reiki (era)|ja|霊亀|lt=Reiki|lt_ja=霊亀}} 2 (716) {{ill|Gyōki|ja|行基|lt=Gyōki|lt_ja=行基}}, an eminent monk of the {{ill|Nara period|ja|奈良時代|lt=Nara period|lt_ja=奈良時代}}, carved an image of {{ill|Bhaisajyaguru|ja|薬師如来|lt=Yakushi|lt_ja=薬師如来}} and enshrined it here.{{sfn|Engishiki Jinja no Chōsa: Ono Jinja}}

In the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代|lt=Kamakura period|lt_ja=鎌倉時代}} the shrine was devoutly worshipped by {{ill|Aikō Suetaka|ja|愛甲季隆|lt=Aikō Saburō Suetaka|lt_ja=愛甲三郎季隆}},<ref>[http://www.tanzawa.or.jp/~sakai/mite03.html Aikō Saburō Suetaka: a tour of his sites] (Mite aruki no ki) {{Broken link|date=2021-10}}</ref> who kept his residence at Aikō village, served three generations of shoguns from {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝|lt=Minamoto no Yoritomo|lt_ja=源頼朝}} on as a {{ill|Gokenin|ja|御家人|lt=gokenin|lt_ja=御家人}}, and was famed as an archer; the whole Aikō family worshipped here. An old dedication tablet records a restoration of the shrine in {{ill|Kenkyū|ja|建久|lt=Kenkyū|lt_ja=建久}} 5 (1194) with Aikō Saburō Suetaka as patron, and also carries the name of Ōe no Kamon-no-taifu Hiromoto ({{ill|Ōe no Hiromoto|ja|大江広元|lt=Ōe no Hiromoto|lt_ja=大江広元}}), head of the {{ill|Kamakura shogunate|ja|鎌倉幕府|lt=Kamakura shogunate|lt_ja=鎌倉幕府}}{{'}}s {{ill|Mandokoro|ja|政所|lt=Mandokoro|lt_ja=政所}}. The shrine buildings have since been rebuilt five times.<ref name="kanajin-ono">[http://www.kanagawa-jinja.or.jp/search_dtl.php4?jid=1042&cd=1207105&scd=&npg=0 Ono Shrine] (Kanagawa Prefecture Jinjachō)</ref> The Yokoyama clan, head family of the Aikō, is said to descend from {{ill|Ono no Imoko|ja|小野妹子|lt=Ono no Imoko|lt_ja=小野妹子}}.<ref name="chigasaki13-onojin" />

[[File:Ono-jin (Atsugi) 3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{ill|Haiden (Shinto)|ja|拝殿|lt=Haiden|lt_ja=拝殿}}]]
At the end of the Edo period the shrine moved a short distance (see [[#Former site|Former site]]), and in {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治|lt=Meiji|lt_ja=明治}} 6 (1873) it was ranked a ''gō-sha''.<ref name="kanajin-ono" /> The haiden had a thatched roof (built {{ill|Kaei|ja|嘉永|lt=Kaei|lt_ja=嘉永}} 1, 1848) until {{ill|Shōwa era|ja|昭和|lt=Shōwa|lt_ja=昭和}} 43 (1968), when it was re-roofed with sheet iron.<ref name="chigasaki13-onojin" />

"Shizuka Daimyōjin", which still survives on the {{ill|Hengaku|ja|扁額|lt=name plaque|lt_ja=扁額}}, was the name used in the Edo period, and the shrine was popularly called "Shizuka-sama" of Ono.{{sfn|Engishiki Jinja no Chōsa: Ono Jinja}} The ''{{ill|Shinpen Sagami no Kuni Fudoki-kō|ja|新編相模国風土記稿|lt=Shinpen Sagami no Kuni Fudoki-kō|lt_ja=新編相模国風土記稿}}'', compiled in the Edo period, shows that the shrine was then called "Shizuka Daimyōjin" and its deity was "{{ill|Shitaharu no Mikoto|ja|下春命|lt=Shitaharu no Mikoto|lt_ja=下春命}}".{{sfn|Shinpen Sagami no Kuni Fudoki-kō: Ono village, Shizuka Daimyōjin}} The deity became Yamato Takeru only in the Meiji period, because the place in the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記|lt=Kojiki|lt_ja=古事記}}'' where {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|lt=Yamato Takeru|lt_ja=日本武尊}} was caught in a set grass fire on his eastern expedition was held to be connected with Ono.<ref name="chigasaki13-onojin" />

== Festivals ==
* 1 January: Gantan-sai (New Year festival)
* 17 February: {{ill|Kinensai|ja|祈年祭|lt=Kinensai|lt_ja=祈年祭}} (spring festival)
* 21 March: spring {{ill|Kōreisai|ja|皇霊祭|lt=Kōreisai|lt_ja=皇霊祭}}
* 21 April: '''{{ill|Reisai|ja|例祭|lt=Reisai|lt_ja=例祭}}''' (great festival)
* 13 July: {{ill|Gion Festival|ja|祇園祭|lt=Gion festival|lt_ja=祇園祭}} ("Tennō-san")
* 23 September: autumn Kōreisai
* 23 November: {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|ja|新嘗祭|lt=Niiname-sai|lt_ja=新嘗祭}} (autumn festival)
* 25 December: {{ill|Ōharae|ja|大祓|lt=Ōharae|lt_ja=大祓}}

== Former site ==
The shrine originally stood on a hill (known as "Kami no Yama", the god's mountain) about 200 metres south-west of the present site. The move is thought to have been at the beginning of the {{ill|Kaei|ja|嘉永|lt=Kaei|lt_ja=嘉永}} era (1848–1854). The hill is now private land, and a small shrine of {{ill|Akiba shrine|ja|秋葉神社|lt=Akiba Shrine|lt_ja=秋葉神社}} stands there in place of Ono Shrine (it was probably built after the move).<ref>[http://d.hatena.ne.jp/x-0/20090704/p1 An old shrine at the foot of Ōyama, Sagami: Ono Shrine (Ono, Atsugi)] (Katsute Nihon to iu kuni ga atta) {{Broken link|date=2021-10}}</ref><ref>[http://www.kaguraden.net/patio/read.cgi?mode=&no=5&p=2 Shikinaisha goshuin information (bulletin board)] (Kantō no jinja meguri Puchi Kaguraden)</ref>

== Access ==
* From {{ill|Hon-Atsugi Station|ja|本厚木駅|lt=Hon-Atsugi Station|lt_ja=本厚木駅}} on the {{ill|Odakyū Odawara Line|ja|小田急小田原線|lt=Odakyū Odawara Line|lt_ja=小田急小田原線}} (Atsugi Bus Center), take a {{ill|Kanagawa Chuo Kotsu|ja|神奈川中央交通|lt=Kanagawa Chūō Kōtsū|lt_ja=神奈川中央交通}} bus (Atsu 43/45, for "Mori no Sato") to "Ono Miyamae", then 3 minutes on foot.

== Nearby ==
The following nine places other than the shrine, temples, shrines, sites and kofun, are introduced on the "Atsugi cultural properties guide board (Furusato jikū tanbō model course)" that the Atsugi City {{ill|Board of education|ja|教育委員会|lt=Board of Education|lt_ja=教育委員会}} has set up in front of the shrine.<ref>[http://merry.whitesnow.jp/BACKNUMBER/20060609/merry.html Furusato jikū tanbō model course] (Merī no heya, 9 June 2006) {{Broken link|date=2021-10}}</ref>
* Komachi Shrine (小町神社): a shrine on top of a small hill in Komachi Green Space, north-west of Ono Shrine, with {{ill|Folklore|ja|伝承|lt=legends|lt_ja=伝承}} about {{ill|Ono no Komachi|ja|小野小町|lt=Ono no Komachi|lt_ja=小野小町}}.
* Koyasu Shrine (子安神社): 379 Okatsuko.
* Ryūtanzan Ryūhō-ji (龍潭山龍鳳寺): 1221 Ono.
* Hōgozan Kisshō-ji (法悟山吉祥寺): 854 Okatsuko; Rinzai school, Nanzen-ji branch.
* Shōunzan Monshū-ji (祥雲山聞修寺): 1201 Ono.
** Wakamiya Hachiman-gū
* Ryūtei Fujō haiku stone (柳亭布丈句碑)
* Okatsuko site (岡津古久遺跡; {{ill|Archaeological excavation|ja|発掘調査|lt=excavated|lt_ja=発掘調査}} in 1974 and later lost to development)
* Shimanokori kofun cluster (島残古墳群)
* Sakon-zuka (左近塚)

== Notes ==
At present the Kumano Shrine at Aikō, Atsugi<ref>[http://www.kanagawa-jinja.or.jp/search_dtl.php4?jid=1036&cd=1207099&scd=000&npg=0 Kumano Shrine] (Kanagawa Prefecture Jinjachō)</ref> also manages Ono Shrine, but as Kumano Shrine is itself often without a priest, it is best to enquire beforehand about {{ill|Goshuin|ja|朱印|lt=goshuin|lt_ja=朱印}} and the like (checked 2 January 2017).
